title: Canada and India review progress on joint roadmap priorities
excerpt: Foreign Affairs Minister Anita Anand met with External Affairs Minister Subrahmanyam Jaishankar in New Delhi to discuss bilateral cooperation.
bodyHtml:
On October 14, 2026, according to the Government of Canada, the Honourable Anita Anand, Minister of Foreign Affairs, met with Minister of External Affairs Subrahmanyam Jaishankar during her visit to India. According to the Government of Canada, the meeting took place to deepen bilateral relations, discuss regional and global issues, and continue to advance Canada-India joint roadmap priorities.

The Government of Canada stated that the ministers discussed the positive momentum in the renewed Canada-India Strategic Partnership. The Government of Canada reported that Minister Anand and Minister Jaishankar reviewed progress made since the launch of the joint roadmap during Minister Anand’s first visit to India a year ago. They discussed ways to further advance roadmap priorities, including trade, energy, people-to-people ties and security and defence cooperation. According to the Government of Canada, the ministers discussed other geopolitical issues, including the Middle East conflict and what the Government of Canada described as the unjustified war in Ukraine.

According to the Government of Canada, the ministers welcomed the recent bilateral security dialogue held in India at the National Security Advisor level, where senior officials from both countries reviewed progress in bilateral security and law enforcement cooperation. The ministers also welcomed efforts to advance negotiations for a comprehensive economic partnership agreement and highlighted the Team Canada Trade Mission led by International Trade Minister Maninder Sidhu. The ministers welcomed upcoming high-level engagements between the two countries to further deepen bilateral ties and agreed to remain in close contact.
